speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Singapore is situated alongside one of the world's busiest waterways and has one of the world's busiest ports.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The Convention provides a set of international rules for State Parties to remove wrecks in their exclusive economic zones (EEZ) that pose a danger to navigation or to the marine environment.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It allows State Parties to recover the costs of locating, marking and removing wrecks from the shipowners.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The Convention also requires State Parties to certify that insurance or other forms of financial security for such liability is in force for ships under their registry.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Clause 8 empowers the Director of Marine of the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) to remove a wreck determined by him to constitute a hazard, if the owner of the wrecked ship fails to undertake the removal or if immediate action is required.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Under the Bill, the Director of Marine must use the most practical and expeditious means available and take into consideration safety of navigation and protection of the marine environment when removing the wreck.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Clause 10 provides for the owner of a ship wrecked in Singapore's EEZ to be liable for the costs of locating, marking and removing the wreck.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Clause 15 stipulates that a ship may not enter or leave the port of Singapore unless it carries on board evidence that it is covered by wreck removal insurance.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Clause 16 provides for the registered owner of a Singapore ship to apply for, and the Director of Marine to issue, certificates to attest that the ship is covered by wreck removal insurance.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Clause 17 provides the Director of Marine with a right of direct action against the insurer of the wrecked ship, for the costs of locating, marking and removing the wreck.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The shipping industry has been consulted and they are supportive of the Bill.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: At the corridor, Mr Louis Ng told me that he supports the Bill but he gave me some feedback from one industry contact.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I assured him that there would be minimal additional administrative and cost burden for shipowners as the application process for the wreck removal certificate is similar to that of other mandatory certificates.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: To further reduce any administrative inconvenience, MPA also has in place processes to renew the Wreck Removal Certificate as a package, together with the statutory certificates required under other international conventions.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: MPA has also checked with the established marine insurance providers and understands that there will be no increase in premium for ships insured with them.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The limits of liability for maritime claims provided by them to their members are already in excess of the limits required under the Convention.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In the event of an incident, MPA will work closely with the shipowner and the insurer from the onset to remove the wreck.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The deadline to remove the wreck will be determined by MPA in consultation with the shipowner and the insurer.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: MPA will only take over the removal of wreck if the shipowner and insurer abandon the wreck or if the wreck constitutes a hazard to navigation or to the marine environment.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In such instances, any surplus from the sale of the wreck will be held in trust.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: MPA will then call for claimants to provide evidence of their entitlement and disburse the surplus to the rightful beneficiary as expeditiously as possible.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Should there be competing claims, MPA will seek the Court's determination.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One, the wreck may be a hazard to navigation, risking the safety of ships and their crew.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Two, the vessel or their cargo may pose environmental risk, for example, pollution to the waters or environment may be caused by bunkers or cargo carried by the vessel.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Three, the costs of marking and removing wrecks have always been an issue.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Provision of compulsory insurance cover aims to deal with this issue of costs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It took about seven years for the Convention to achieve the requisite number of ratifications, which was the number of 10 countries from around the world triggering the entry into force conditions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As a result, amongst the states which had ratified it earlier, the Convention entered into force on 14 April 2015.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It will also provide states with a right of direct action against insurers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Ships are also required under the Convention to obtain a certificate from a state which is party to the Convention, attesting that such insurance is in place for each vessel.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such state certificate must be carried on board the vessel.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The good news is that the insurance cover required has been made readily available by the key Protection and Indemnity (P&I) clubs within the International Group in the world, and this made for easier compliance for all ships and their registered owners, albeit adding to the costs of doing business.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Vessels registered in a state which is not party to the Convention but which perform voyages to countries which are parties to the Convention must obtain a certificate from a State Party.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In fact, between 2015 and the present date, as Singapore delayed in its ratification of the Convention, MPA had issued an advisory to ships registered under the Singapore flag to obtain such certificates from other countries which have ratified the Convention earlier.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the issue of penalties listed under sections 4, 15, 23 and 31 of the Bill, I am concerned whether the recommended maximum fines are sufficient to deter reporting or other offences.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I note from an MPA circular of 2015 that preparations were being made to legislation to implement this convention and MPA directed the Singapore-flagged ships to the United Kingdom, Denmark, Germany, Marshall Islands, Liberia and Cook Islands for the issuance of the State Certificates.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These countries had ratified the Convention before the Convention came into force.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Notwithstanding the above, I am in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is not unusual for countries to take time to accede to a convention.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For this particular Bill, time was needed to consult the various stakeholders, and we wanted to make sure that it is something that the industry supports and owns the decision.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In this instance, even though we take a few years, we are still among the earliest to have done so.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think, as of to date, less than 30 countries have acceded to the Convention, out of about 200 countries in the world, and, in Asia, we would be among the first.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As for the question on penalties, MPA have assessed them to be adequate.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They have taken into account the other penalties imposed by the other sections of the Bill.
